title: Fabius the Delayer
objective: After this level you can explain Fabius Maximus’s strategy of avoiding battle and why it worked.
summary: Fabius shadowed Hannibal and cut his supplies instead of fighting. Mocked as the Delayer, he was proved right as Italy’s allies held firm.

cards.headline: Sometimes the best way to beat a genius is to refuse to fight him.
Don’t fight, follow
cards.body: Fabius Maximus refused to meet Hannibal in a pitched battle. Instead he shadowed Hannibal’s army and cut off its supplies. Romans first mocked him as Cunctator, “the Delayer.” After Cannae, the name became praise.

cards.headline: Why it worked
cards.body: Hannibal was far from home and needed Italian cities to join him. But most of Rome’s allies stayed loyal, so he never got the reinforcements he needed. Time, and Hannibal’s distance from home, were on Rome’s side.

cards.context: A “Fabian strategy” still means wearing down a stronger enemy by avoiding a decisive battle, exactly as Fabius did.

cards.headline: Delay: vindicated
learned: He cut off Hannibal’s supplies instead
Italy’s loyal allies starved Hannibal of men

questions.prompt: What nickname did Fabius Maximus earn?

options.label: The Conqueror
options.rationale: His fame came from not fighting.

questions.explanation: Cunctator, “the Delayer,” began as an insult and became praise.

questions.prompt: Why did avoiding battle hurt Hannibal?

options.label: His elephants needed battles to stay fit
options.rationale: The issue was supplies and allies.

options.label: Far from home, he needed supplies and new allies
Roman law forbade him to march
His soldiers were paid only after victories
options.rationale: The issue was supplies and allies.

questions.explanation: Without battles to win over Italian cities, Hannibal’s army slowly ran short of supplies and men.

questions.prompt: From Level 19: what Roman policy helped Fabius’s strategy work?

options.label: Turning defeated Italians into loyal allies
Building walls around every Italian town
Keeping the navy in harbor
options.rationale: The key was allies on land.

questions.explanation: Rome had made defeated peoples allies; most stayed loyal, so Hannibal couldn’t replace his losses.
